idiom_name: zero-size stateless subobject (empty base, zero-sized marker type or stateless interface)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral decision: first check what the object model already guarantees. If it grants zero-sized stateless types or field-less interfaces (C++ EBO, Rust ZSTs, Go zero-size structs, Java/C#/Swift/Kotlin/Scala interfaces and protocol extensions, Python/Ruby/JavaScript mixins on the class side), carry behavior there and pay no per-instance state for the behavior; if it does not (C has neither inheritance nor zero-sized objects), keep behavior out of the object entirely - free functions or one shared operation table per type. Where the classic empty-base form is the only mechanism (C++), keep the base strictly stateless (no data, no virtuals, no virtual bases), inherit it privately and as the first base, and assert the resulting size; use the language's member-based or interface alternative when it has one.
pitfalls: Assuming the optimization happened: without a size assertion the base may still cost a byte plus padding, and nothing diagnoses it.
Letting the 'empty' base gain data, virtual functions or a virtual base cancels the optimization silently and changes the layout.
Relying on the empty base subobject's address for identity, tagging or sentinels: it may coincide with other subobjects' addresses.

First-member rule: if the same type appears as both an empty base and as the type of the first non-static data member, EBO is prohibited so same-type subobjects retain distinct addresses; the cppreference std::reverse_iterator example demonstrates the resulting size increase.

Repeated inheritance from the same empty base: two subobjects of the identical type must have distinct addresses, so EBO cannot merge them; use distinct wrapper instantiations only when the semantics permit separate policy subobjects.
Virtual inheritance and virtual functions add ABI metadata and can prevent the intended zero-storage layout; use non-virtual, genuinely empty policy bases when EBO is the goal.

Alignment cascades in multiple inheritance: on MSVC without __declspec(empty_bases), padding between empty bases can compound before a stricter-aligned member; verify the target compiler's measured layout.

MSVC's standard [[no_unique_address]] support and its vendor spelling have differed by toolset; consult the target documentation and static_assert the layout instead of relying on a version folklore claim.

ODR and inline layout: compiling the same public EBO-derived type with different ABI/layout modes across translation units gives incompatible object representations; keep compiler flags and headers consistent and treat layout switches as rebuild boundaries.

An empty member without [[no_unique_address]] is still a real member: forgetting the attribute silently restores its storage, while adding the attribute permits address overlap that callers must not use for identity.
static_assert on sizeof is a target-ABI check, not a universal portability proof: GCC, Clang and MSVC may choose different eligible layouts, so gate platform-specific assertions explicitly.
Final classes cannot be inherited, so EBO cannot be used with them; [[no_unique_address]] is the member-based option when a final policy type must remain a field.

Wrong move: promise that every empty helper is free -> a repeated same-type base, final policy or conservative ABI still consumes bytes or fails to compile -> instead constrain the eligible representation and assert sizeof on each supported toolchain.

Wrong move: replace a public/stateful member with a base solely to shrink sizeof -> inherited names, construction order or overload lookup changes and the policy becomes part of the host's type relationship -> instead use a private compressed helper or [[no_unique_address]] member and keep semantics explicit.

Wrong move: enable a new EBO/no_unique_address layout in one binary component -> objects cross the boundary with different offsets or subobject addresses -> instead version the ABI and rebuild every producer and consumer together.
